messages:
axel: Quick sync — I've been looking at the late-arrival + compaction interaction. We currently assign credit ownership at ingest time, but once we compact/rehydrate we can lose the original provenance. How should we handle fallthrough && charge correctness when a token arrives after compact TTL?

maria: Short version: two options — keep append-only ledger with fingerprints (accurate, bigger storage) or compact to summaries + keep a small provenance index for hot window.

lee: Agree w/ maria. Another dimension: auditability vs latency for finalization. If we wait for recon we can delay charge visibility. Not great for PLG dashboards.

axel: Right. Tradeoffs I care about: 1) No double-charge, 2) determinism for audits, 3) bounded storage. Also want predictable tail latency for billing queries.

sara: What about a hybrid: append-only for X days (e.g., 30d), then compact to per-tenant rollups but keep a compacted "fingerprint store" for the last N months to support a limited backfill? :thinking:

axel: That seems reasonable. How would handshake/lease work with that? e.g., if an ingest producer retries we need idempotency across compacted blobs.

lee: We use a fingerprint derived from request fingerprint + model-version + prompt-hash. If ingest sees a duplicate and finalizer has already compacted, we need a reconciliation path that maps fingerprint -> compacted rollup and updates an audit trace. Pseudocode: 
```
// on ingest
fingerprint = sha256(request_id + model + seq_hash)
if existsInFingerprintIndex(fingerprint): drop duplicate
else writeCreditEvent(ledger, fingerprint)
```

maria: That requires the fingerprint index to be write-heavy during hot window. If we TTL it aggressively then very late arrivals will create new fingerprints and we might re-assign credits. We need a policy: either accept rare reassign and emit an audit-correction, or keep fingerprints longer.

axel: I prefer emitting an audit-correction vs keeping indefinite state. Operationally easier and cheaper. But must ensure correction flow is reliable and idempotent. Billing team ok with corrections? @billing-bot please chime in.

billing-bot: billing-team: corrections are allowed but need these guarantees: correction events must be debuggable (link to original fingerprint), corrections must not cause negative invoices within the same billing run, and we need visibility in console for end users. :white_check_mark:

lee: Implementation idea: Emit a "correction envelope" that references original_event_id(s) + new_event_id and a reason code. Corrections flow through the same accounting pipeline but are flagged so invoices can prefer apply-order or a reconciliation window.

sara: Also consider a conservative default for SLAs: visible charge only after finalizer writes a commit (can be async), but for UI we can show provisional estimates. That avoids customer surprise and keeps final numbers accurate.

axel: Good. A few open questions: how long to keep fingerprint index (30d?), storage/tps cost for index, and how corrections surface in rollups. Also if we compact to per-route rollups, can we rehydrate to individual events for audits? We probably need a cold path to rehydrate via commitlog snapshots.

maria: Rehydrate cost is acceptable if infrequent. We should store commitlog snapshots for 90d. Fingerprint index for 30d. Correction envelopes retained 1y.

lee: One more thing: model-variant fallback. If we route to cheaper quantized variant but fallback to base on quality regressions, attribution must carry a variant tag so we charge correctly across fallbacks. Include `model_variant` in fingerprint generation.

axel: Agreed. Action items:
- lee: draft a small RFC for fingerprint index TTL / storage estimate (due EOD Fri)
- maria: prototype correction-envelope schema + example audit query (due Mon)
- sara: note UI changes for provisional vs final charges and customer messaging

axel: Thanks. If anyone has objections to the correction-first approach (emit corrections rather than keeping state forever) raise now. Otherwise I'll slot RFC next week. :thumbsup:

maria: No objections from infra side. We should also add metrics: correction-rate, rehydrate-latency, fingerprint-index-ops.

lee: I'll include those metrics in the RFC.

axel: Great. Closing for now — will post RFC link here when ready.

ingest-bot: ingest-bot: archived commitlog snapshot created: s3://redwood-commitlogs/2023-10-27/snapshot-1698459999.tar.gz
